summary: Iteration 1 achieved a score of 78.9/100, a major jump from the 33.5 baseline, by implementing SA with NN-guided 2-opt and an efficient penalty delta computation that only checks every-10th-step positions. The key insight was that penalty recomputation for a reversed segment is O(segment/10), not O(segment), enabling much larger 2-opt moves within the 2-second time budget.
key_points: Score improved from 0 (sequential baseline) → 33.5 (NN + limited SA) → 78.9 (NN-guided 2-opt with efficient delta), confirming that move selection targeting spatially-close but tour-distant city pairs is highly productive.

Still ~21 points of headroom remain. Unknown whether this gap is from suboptimal construction, insufficient SA iterations, missing move types (Or-opt, 3-opt), or underexploited prime scheduling at penalty positions.

Next iteration should investigate: (1) Or-opt/relocate moves alongside 2-opt to escape local minima, (2) explicit prime-city scheduling to place primes at every-10th positions as a post-optimization pass, (3) tuning SA temperature schedule and iteration count to maximize improvement within the 2s budget, (4) potentially a better initial tour (e.g., greedy edge insertion instead of NN).
